articleTitle: An Inverter-based Lightweight Digital True Random Number Generator Circuit for IoT Device
abstract: An inverter-based lightweight digital true random number generator (DTRNG) circuit is proposed and verified in silicon. The entropy of inverter jitter is discussed and extracted. The proposed DTRNG circuit uses 8MHz clock and standard digital cell library which is suitable for IoT device with limited area and low working frequency, and it can be easily ported to other process platforms.

articleTitle: Behavioral Modeling of A High-Resolution Sigma-Delta ADC
abstract: A 24-bit high-resolution sigma-delta ADC system structure is present in the paper, which is designed by adopting oversampling technology and noise shaping technology and simulated in Simulink. A modulator structure with OSR = 128, 6th order, single loop, feedforward and one bit quantization are realized. The modulator coefficients are obtained by Matlab. In the Simulink ideal model, the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) can reach 148.5dB. Considering the non-ideal factors such as KT/C noise, clock jitter and operational amplifier noise, the SNR is 126dB. The 24-bit high-resolution sigma-delta ADC can satisfy a variety of industrial measurement scenarios (such as temperature measurement, pressure measurement, industrial automation monitoring, etc.) and medical applications (ECG measurement, EEG measurement, telemedicine, etc.).

articleTitle: Simulation of electrolytic capacitance for the oxide-based electric-double-layer transistors
abstract: The recent advancement of oxide-based electric-double-layer transistors (EDLTs) is exciting in many aspects, but further development requires a better understanding of their physical nature. Since the electrolytic capacitance dominates the unique properties of EDLTs, its understanding has become a critical issue in this area. This study simulated electrolytic capacitance using the ion drift-diffusion model and compared it with actual measured data. Ion concentration was identified as the most significant factor affecting the quasi-static EDL capacitance. And in addition to that, ion diffusion coefficient and electrolyte thickness also impact the frequency dependence of the EDL capacitance and, consequently, the transient response of EDLTs.

articleTitle: Metamaterial-Inspired Microwave Sensor for Ethanol Detection
abstract: In this work, a high-sensitive microwave sensor based on an improved split ring resonator (SRR) for detecting ethanol concentration in aqueous ethanol solutions is proposed. This biosensor combines SRR with the inter-digital capacitor (IDC) and adds two pairs of IDCs on the resonator for enhanced electric field concentration over a larger surface area, which provides higher sensitivity for testing dielectric liquids. The coupling between the two resonant elements and the transmission line deepens the amplitude of the biosensor. The material under test (MUT) is properly placed in the IDC region of the SRR, where the highest electric field strength can achieve low-cost, pollution-free, non-contact, high-sensitivity detection. This sensor resonates at3.44GHz with a resonance amplitude of -17dB. Ethanol in the concentration range of 20%-100% can be measured by the resonant frequency and the S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf> parameter’s change. The sensitivity of this microwave sensor for measuring ethanol is 0.75 MHz/% and 0.03 dB/%, which can be used for quantitative detection of ethanol solution.

articleTitle: A Sidewall Enhanced Trench Poly-Si/SiC Heterojunction Diode with Energy Barrier Height Control Technology
abstract: Silicon carbide power diodes are widely used in various power electronic systems due to their low losses. In the conventional SiC Schottky diodes, the forward voltage drops mainly depends on the work function of the anode metal material, which brings constraints to the design of SiC Schottky diodes. For the proposed poly-Si/SiC heterojunction diode (HJD), the barrier height and forward voltage drop can be optimized by adjusting the polysilicon doping type and concentration. And the trade-off relationship between the on-state conduction loss and off-state loss (leakage current) also can be improved according to different applications. In this paper, a novel sidewall enhanced trench HJD is proposed to achieve extremely low leakage current under the premise of high forward current density and low on-voltage drop, which brings a new design method for the SiC power diodes.

articleTitle: High quality factor microwave sensor for ethanol solution concentration detection
abstract: When using microwave sensors to detect the concentration of a solution, two important objectives to consider are resolution and sensitivity. This paper presents a bent-wire based microwave sensor that combined an active feedback loop to increase the quality factor from 47 to 295. The external capacitance changes the resonant frequency to study the influence on the detection sensitivity. The resonant frequency of the active microwave sensor gradually increased from 2.62GHz to 3.10GHz with capacitance of $24\mathrm{pF},2.4\mathrm{pF}$, and 1pF respectively. The resonant frequency without external capacitor is 2.26 GHz. Active microwave sensors at four resonant frequencies were used for sensing ethanol solutions from 0 to $ 100\%$ concentration. When characterized by frequency shift, the sensitivity increased from $ 0.17\mathrm{MHz}/\%$ to $ 0.34\mathrm{MHz}/\%$ with increasing frequency, and when characterized by magnitude change, the sensitivity peaked at $ 0.14\mathrm{~dB}/\%$ at the detection frequency of 2.62GHz, in agreement with the theoretical analysis. This result shows that active microwave sensors, combined with the frequency correction effect of chip capacitors, can effectively improve sensing sensitivity.

articleTitle: A Low-Power SAR ADC with Multi-mode Switching Scheme
abstract: This paper proposes an energy-efficient switching scheme for successive approximation register analog-to-digital converter (SAR ADC). This switching scheme adopts constraint bit control and asynchronous SAR logic to reduce the area and power consumption of ADC. The combination of top-plate sampling, monotonic switching and multiple reference voltages prevents the capacitor array from generating dynamic power consumption in the first three comparison stages. In the subsequent comparison stages, the difference of bottom-plate voltage switching under the corresponding weight-bit capacitance is only 1/4$V_{\mathrm{ref}}$. Compared with the conventional scheme, the proposed scheme saves 99.61% of the average dynamic power consumption and reduces the total capacitance by 87.5%. An asynchronous 8-bit SAR ADC based on the proposed scheme is implemented in a 65 nm CMOS technology. At 1.2 V power supply voltage and 5 MS/s input sampling rate, the power consumption of SAR ADC is 25 μW and the FOM is 22.1 fJ/Conv.

articleTitle: An Ultra-wideband Bandpass Filter Based on Half-mode Substrate Integrated Waveguide Loaded with Rectangular-ring Slot
abstract: An ultra-wideband bandpass filter based on half-mode substrate integrated waveguide design is proposed. This bandpass filter is designed on a Rogers RO4350 dielectric substrate. The rectangular slot is used to achieve fast attenuation of high-frequency edge of passband, and the characteristic of out-of-band harmonic suppression can be adjusted by changing the position of the rectangular slot. The 3D electromagnetic simulation software HFSS is used to simulate the proposed filter. From the simulation results, the center frequency of the filter is 11.64 GHz, and the 3 dB fractional bandwidth is 119.2 % from 4.7 GHz to 18.58 GHz. The insertion loss is better than 0.3 dB and return loss is better than 20 dB in the passband.

articleTitle: A Wide IF Baseband-Noise-Cancelling CMOS Analog Receiver with Current-Mirror TIA
abstract: by using a baseband noise cancellation, a CMOS mixer-first analog receiver with power reduction is proposed. Based on a current-mirror TIA structure, positive capacitive feedback is applied to manipulate poles/zeros location, enabling a wide baseband bandwidth and out-of-band second-order filtering profile. The additional radio frequency N-path filtering and baseband 40dB/dec roll-off supress out-of-band interferences. The presented frontend is designed in 65 nm CMOS. Simulations demonstrate a minimal noise figure of 2.0 dB, and a voltage gain of 32.5 dB across the 220 MHz intermediate frequency range. The in-band (IB) and out-of-band (OOB) IIP3 manifests −12.5/15 dBm. The receiver circuit draws 27.4 mW at a typical 1 GHz LO stimulus.

articleTitle: Experimental Investigations on the Impedance Characteristics of the Gas Sensors
abstract: For commonly-used gas sensors, their resistance characteristics are mostly exploited for gas detection and identification. However, in practical, the gas sensors exhibit complicated impedance characteristics which probably include resistive, capacitive and inductive response during the inter-reaction between the gas molecules and the sensing materials. We designed and built a dedicated measurement system based on the frequency scanning method for the research of the impedance characteristics of the gas sensors. 11 types of commercial gas sensors were chosen, and their impedance characteristics in response to the ethanol and the acetone were measured separately. We analyzed the frequency response, the concentration response and the corresponding trends according the measurement results.

articleTitle: High Isolation Integrated Passive Micro-Diplexer with Low Loss for Mobile Communication Applications
abstract: In this paper, a high isolation and low loss integrated passive micro-diplexer is designed through different combinations of inductors and capacitors. The design of the micro-diplexer uses the structure of a toroidal inductor and a metal-dielectric-metal type capacitor, and an air bridge structure is arranged at the port of the toroidal inductor. The air bridge structure is composed of multiple layers of metal and it provides a new way for the parallel connection of the inductor and the capacitor, which reduces the size of the micro-diplexer and improves the integration of the micro-diplexer. The proposed micro-diplexer realizes high-isolation communication and low-loss signal transmission at the operating frequency of 0.900 GHz and 1.800 GHz, respectively. And the insertion losses are 0.003 dB and 0.001 dB, the isolation degrees are 39.439 dB and 43.197 dB, respectively. In summary, the proposed micro-diplexer can be easily integrated with other devices through bond-wires, which is beneficial to improve the integration of radio frequency circuits. Moreover, it provides an effective solution for electronic devices to share a common communication channel, which is helpful to promote the exploration and application of micro-diplexer in duplex communication.

articleTitle: Effect of Layout Shape on the Performance of OCSRR Microwave Sensor
abstract: Microwave sensors based on open complementary spilt ring resonator (OCSRR) structures have been widely studied and applied because of their small electrical size, they are also very sensitive to dielectric loading. The purpose of this paper is to study OCSRR microwave sensors based on different shapes (square, round and trapezoid), using resonant frequency f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> as well as return loss Sll to characterize the dielectric properties of ethanol solutions when the other variables (overall area, channel length and channel gap, etc.) are the same as well as the resonant frequency. From the results, the sensitivity of the square structure of the OCSRR microwave sensor is the highest, 0.16 MHz/% and 0.084 dB/%, respectively, whether the sensitivity is calculated based on the resonant frequency or the change in return loss amplitude. This is because, on the one hand, the square structure of the OCSRR microwave sensor accumulates more electric field energy than the round and trapezoid; on the other hand, the quality factor of the square structure of the OCSRR microwave sensor is higher than those of the round and trapezoid.

articleTitle: Research On AT697 Chip Cache Anti-SEU Hardened Technology
abstract: The AT697 chip is a common aerospace main controller chip, but abnormality detection mechanism of AT697 chip only supports parity check function, it is easy to cause uncorrectable error due to SEU (single event upset), which leads to task failure. To solve this problem, the paper implements a kind of cache Anti-SEU hardened technology, it can clear single bit error in cache due to SEU in time. The paper also introduces a novel SEU error injection method, which can verify robustness and effectiveness of Anti-SEU hardened technology efficiently. By using SEU error injection method, experiment compares SEU counts before and after applying Anti-SEU hardened technology. Result shows significant effect of hardened technology on eliminating cache SEU.

articleTitle: A Universal Core Surface-Potential Modeling Methodology for Future Heterogeneous AOS/Si Co-integrated Design
abstract: A universal core surface potential modeling methodology is proposed to obtain the continuous explicit solutions to Poisson equation for future heterogeneous AOS/Si co-integrated design, without the necessity to solve implicit equations by numerical iteration or the table lookup method as previous work. This method is compatible to devices with various structures and different channel materials. In this paper, it has been successfully applied to Bulk MOSFET, SOI MOSFET and IGZO-based MOSFET. The fully analytical solutions of the surface potential will contribute to compact expressions of drain current, terminal charge and capacitance, incorporating physics-based and structural parameters. Thus, such a unified high accuracy and efficiency methodology is suitable for surface potential compact model towards future multi-functional heterogeneous integrated circuit design.

articleTitle: A novel high-precision compact SCR model for ESD protection circuit simulation using SPICE
abstract: In this paper, we present a novel compact physical model for the silicon-controlled-rectifier (SCR), which incorporates multiple secondary effects within the device, along with an improved E-M model for the bipolar junction transistor (BJT). Our model is designed to work with current electronic design automation (EDA) simulation tools, and its accuracy is demonstrated through consistent simulation results with measured results of the SCR under 0.18$\mu$m BCD. Compared to previous models, the proposed model exhibits enhanced precision, and its layout parameters can be adjusted to suit different EDA simulation tool environments.

articleTitle: The method of improving data retention for Logic Flash
abstract: The study aims to investigate the method of improving data retention for logic flash by studying different process condition and analyzing how much current drops after 250C baking times in details. According to the experimental results, it is shown that not only the material and thickness of HTO and gate oxide capacitor, but also process thermal and wet chemical have influence to data retention for logic flash.

articleTitle: Design and optimization of lead-forming for CFP package based on finite element analysis
abstract: With the development and application of ceramic packages, the thermal fatigue failure, which comes from the mismatch of thermal expansion coefficient (CTE) between different materials, becomes one of the main failures to modules during temperature cycling. In this paper, the model of a typical assembling module, which includes a ceramic flat package (CFP) soldered on the PCB, was established. And then, the finite element analysis software was used to simulate the thermal stress of solders and leads in the assembling module.To analyze the effect of the lead-forming parameters, the shoulder, the height and the angle were selected as analysis variables. Then, a series of forming parameter combinations was designed. Accordingly, all the over-molded assembling modules were simulated in the same thermal condition to analyze the trends of the stress. Based on the simulation results and actual lead-forming condition, a better combination of lead-forming parameters which resulting in the minimum stress of solders was chose as the final scheme. Comparing with the typical assembling module, the maximum stress of the solders in the final scheme decreases 1.8MPa (5.7%), and the maximum stress of the lead decreases 55.4MPa (37.9%).Generally, the possible failure point during the temperature cycling is on the solder. The fatigue life of the solder joint was calculated using Engelmaier’s model. Lastly, the simulation and experiment results show that the final lead-forming scheme meets the application environment and realizes the structure optimization of CFP16 package well.

articleTitle: Design of A Fast Transient Response Capacitor-Less LDO with Dual Loop
abstract: This paper presents a fast transient response low- dropout regulator (LDO) with enhanced slew rate and no off-chip capacitor for system-on-chip (SOC) applications. The LDO regulator uses a combination of a folded-cascode operational amplifier and a transient-enhanced circuit to drive the PMOS pass element. The transient enhanced circuit can improve the slew rate of power element. The introduction of a dual-loop feedback loop architecture can further improve transient response. The proposed LDO is simulated based on SK 0.1S$\mu$m standard CMOS process. The result shows that when the input voltage is 2.1V, the output voltage is 1.SV, and the quiescent current is 37$\mu$A. Loop stability can be maintained with a load capacitance of only 10 pF and a maximum load of 50 mA. When the load current changes from 1mA to 50mA within 10ns, the undershoot and overshoot response times are 98ps and 97ps, respectively, where the best 0.075 ps FOM is achieved.

articleTitle: ESD Characteristics Improving for DDSCR with NBL by Adding High Voltage N-type Well Isolation in 0.18-μm BCD Technology
abstract: This paper investigates the effect of High Voltage N-type Well layer (HVNW) on the trigger voltage, holding voltage and failure current of dual directional Silicon-Controlled Rectifier with N-type Buried Layer (DDSCR-NBL) devices. The DDSCR with N-type buried layer (DDSCR-NBL) and the DDSCR-HVNW are fabricated on a $0.18-\mu m$ Bipolar CMOS DMOS (BCD) technology. A transmission line pulse (TLP) testing system and a 2-dimension device simulation platform have been used in this work. According to the measurement results, the holding voltage $(V_{h})$ and failure current $(I_{t2})$ of the DDSCR-HVNW can be drastically improved by adding HVNW. It can achieve sharply increasing the failure current to be more than 20A and slightly elevating the holding voltage to be more than 30V.

articleTitle: A Low-Loss and High Phase Matching Balun Chip Based on Integrated Passive Technology for S-band RF System
abstract: With the rapid development of 5G and mobile wireless communication systems, the market demand for high-performance RF front-end devices is increasing dramatically. As a balanced-unbalanced signal converter, the balun has attracted the attention of many researchers because of its widely-used advantages in various circuit systems. In this paper, we propose a miniaturized RF balun chip based on integrated passive technology, which can transmit signals in two different transmission environments with less loss. The designed balun chip consists of a T-type lowpass filter, a $\pi-$type highpass filter, transmission line, and coplanar waveguide feedline. The cut-off frequency of the T-type lowpass filter is larger than that of the $\pi-$type highpass filter, so the input signal can pass through the T-type lowpass filter and the $\pi-$type highpass filter to complete the transmission of the balanced signal to two unbalanced signals with a phase difference of 180° in microwave frequency band. The combination of T-type and $\pi$-type filters can reduce the phase mismatch and misalignment, reduce the layout area, which are conducive to miniaturized design and improve the transmission performance. Simulation results indicate the insertion loss is low to -35.56dB in 2.4 GHz, and the die is only 940 $\mu \mathrm{m}\times 907\mu \mathrm{m}$. The RF balun chip based on the integrated passive process proposed in this paper can be applied to the S-band RF system and effectively integrated into active or passive circuit systems.

articleTitle: A Novel SA-LIGBT with Dielectric Isolation
abstract: A novel shorted-anode lateral insulated gate bipolar transistor with dielectric isolation (DI-SA LIGBT) is proposed in this paper. The DI-SA structure is formed by introducing a dielectric trench between P+ and N+in the SA devices. The DISA structure isolation consists of vertical and lateral parts. The lateral dielectric isolation trench increases the anode current path, reduces the resistance ratio between the drift region and the collector, and effectively suppresses the snapback phenomenon in the SA LIGBT unipolar-to-bipolar mode. In the DI-SA LIGBT structure, the snapback and switching speed of the device can be optimized by adjusting the width and length of the vertical and lateral dielectric isolation trench. This paper compares the controllable advantages of DISA LIGBT and conventional SA LIGBT through Technology Computer-Aided Design (TCAD) simulation.

articleTitle: Strain and its effect on optical properties of AlGaN-based DUV LEDs grown on sapphire substrates by MOCVD with different thickness of p-type layers
abstract: The effects of the combined thickness of p-type layers on the strain distribution, optical properties, and the performance of AlGaN-based deep ultraviolet light emitting diodes (DUV LEDs) have been investigated. The results indicate that the accumulation of compressive strain relaxed by the way of dislocation formation during islands coalescence, resulting in a deterioration of crystalline quality. In addition, the shift of the peak wavelength was related to the change in the compressive strain state. Finally, the packaged DUV LED ($\lambda$=275nm) with the $\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{f}}$=6.34V at 50 mA was presented and the light output power of more than 7 mW at 160 mA was achieved at room temperature.

articleTitle: A 1.4-μm pixel-pitch high-speed floating-gate image sensor with a temperature self-correction circuit
abstract: A high-speed floating-gate image sensor with a self-correction circuit has been proposed. The reference voltages are generated for the ramp circuit, having the same temperature characteristics as the threshold voltage of pixel units. At the same time, the integration time is consistent with that at normal temperature (27°C). Thus, the range of the ramp voltage can be dynamically adjusted with temperature changes. Additionally, the frame rate of the image sensor is greatly improved by using the bilateral column readout circuits and compact timing design. Simulation results show that when the temperature changes from −30°C to 125°C, the output voltage error of the sensor can be reduced to less than 1 mV, and the frame rate can reach 122 fps.

articleTitle: Analysis of the impact of modifications on the performance of graphene nanoribbon field effect transistors
abstract: The graphene-based transistors are considered as the potential candidates for low-power design for future nanoelectronics application. In this paper, graphene nanoribbons (GNRs) and graphene nanoribbon field effect transistors (GNRFET) are studied by simulation. The band structure and electronic properties of graphene nanoribbons under different chirality are simulated using tight binding theory. Then, based on the theoretical framework of non-equilibrium Green’s function, the electronic and transport characteristics of double-gate (DG) armchair GNRFET are studied with the change of device structural parameters such as AGNR chirality, gate oxide thickness and dielectric constant. Moreover, the device performance metrics such as subthreshold slope and drain induced barrier lowering (DIBL) effect are analyzed emphatically. This work presents an advance in the understanding of the GNRFET structure with important implications toward the device design.

articleTitle: A High-Speed and Fully Symmetric Time-to-Digital Converter with Picosecond Resolution
abstract: This paper presents the design of a high-resolution time-to-digital converter (TDC) which uses a fully symmetric sense-amplifier-based flip-flop (SAFF) with improved delay chains. Simulation results show that the proposed flip-flop has a small metastability window compared with the other SAFFs. Additionally, the delay and the power are smaller. A high-speed Vernier TDC is also proposed with time resolution of 2. 5ps based on the novel SAFF.

articleTitle: A Low Power, PVT-Resilient LVDS Transmitter
abstract: With the growing demand for high-speed interfaces, low voltage differential signaling (LVDS), has been widely used in high-speed transmission due to its power efficiency and high resilience to noise. This paper presents a new topology of transmitter with an amplitude regulator. The regulator senses the current of current source and feeds it back to regulate the current, and further stabilizes the differential voltage around 350 mV with process, voltage, and temperature (PVT) variations. The other negative feedback loop, consisting of an amplifier and resistors, is also used to regulate the common-mode voltage of the transmitter to 1.24 V. Related voltage biases are provided by a PVT-resilient bandgap voltage reference. A Pre-driver circuit is introduced to make the transmitter work properly at a lower power supply and thus decrease the general power consumption of the whole circuit. Simulation results show that the transmitter works stably with different PVT variations at a speed of 500 MHz.

articleTitle: A Novel SOI LDMOS with Folded Charge Trench
abstract: A novel silicon-on-insulator lateral double diffused metal oxide semiconductor with folded charge trench (FCT-SOI LDMOS) is proposed in this paper. The FCT-SOI is formed by introducing a row of folded charge trench on the buried oxide layer (BOX). The FCT-SOI structure can prevent the inversion layer charges of SOI from being expanded and extracted by the source depletion region, and the inversion layer charges fixed at the BOX interface can not only shield the power lines from the drain substrate to relieve the electric field peak at the drain, but also the electric field enhancement inside the BOX is guided by the interfacial Gauss’s theorem. In addition, the FCT-SOI structure additionally introduces a dielectric electric field in the drift region, realizing dual enhanced dielectric field (ENDIF) in SOI devices. FCT is suitable for high-voltage thick-film SOI devices, the folded charge trench is introduced at the bottom of the drift region, the current transport of the device is hardly affected, the breakdown voltage (BV) can be greatly increased without affecting the drift region resistance of the device. In this paper, the advantages of the breakdown voltage and current after the introduction of the FCT-SOI structure are analyzed and compared in same SOI film thickness devices.

articleTitle: Research on SiP Assessment Methods for High Reliability Applications
abstract: System-in-package (SiP) is an integrated device with low profile, high integration, and diversified functions, suitable for high-reliability application scenarios such as satellites. SiP devices operate in rapid high and low temperature changes, long-term high temperature environment, severe vibration and shock. The reliability of SiP device operating in space is the most important issue. Generally, Sip consists of three-dimensional stacked structure, which includes multiple interfaces such as silicon-silicon and silicon-ceramic. Complex interfaces mean thermal management problems. Electromagnetic coupling effects occur in vertical interconnections and high-density bonding wires. Fine pitch bumps and solder balls face with structural and interface degradation problems caused by electro-thermal coupling stress. This paper analyzes the difficulties of reliability evaluation of SiP for high reliability applications, and proposes a reliability evaluation method based on the process. Simulation and structure analysis are carried out to investigate reliability evaluation technology.

articleTitle: High-Sensitive Microwave Humidity Sensor based on PAN and MXene
abstract: Currently, most humidity sensors have low sensitivity to detect low relative humidity. Therefore, it is necessary to optimize microwave sensor devices and moisture sensitive materials in concert to achieve high sensitivity for low relative humidity detection. In this paper, we propose a miniaturized, high-sensitivity microwave humidity sensor for humidity detection. A complementary split ring resonator (CSRR) is used as the detection electrode. Its high-field region is located in a large copper layer, providing an excellent receiving plane for electrostatic rotation. Therefore, we prepared a moisture-sensitive film of polyacrylonitrile (PAN) with good mechanical stability and water insolubility directly on its surface, compounded both materials by drop coating with an ethanol suspension of MXene, and then characterized relative humidity using the S - parameter. Experimental results indicate a sensitivity of 0.055 dB/% RH in low humidity environments, characterized by an amplitude shift from 10% RH to 70% RH for relative humidity. The sensor achieves high sensitivity in low humidity environments, with its resonant frequency moving less at different humidity levels, and a sensitivity of 0.065 dB/% RH at 2.865 GHz. The sensor is thus potentially useful for future implementations of low-cost microwave humidity sensors in conjunction with fixed-frequency detection circuits.

articleTitle: Low Trigger-Voltage Design of SCR Structure with Power-Rail ESD Clamp Circuit Network for On-Chip ESD Protection
abstract: In this paper, a novel method of deep reducing triggering voltage for silicon controlled rectifier(SCR) with detection circuit has been proposed and verified under a 0.25-μm 5-V Bipolar-CMOS-DMOS (BCD, Complementary and Double-diffused Metal Oxide Semiconductor) process. Its ESD performance is predicted and confirmed through two-dimensional device simulations and Transmission Line Pulse (TLP) test results. From measured results, this Zener diode triggering SCR with a positive injection doping (P+) Trigger Spot (ZDTSCR_P+) decreases trigger voltage from 32.39 V to 7. S2V and increases its holding voltage from 3.12 V to 6.62 V compared with conventional SCR. The ZDTSCRP+ features a narrow ESD window of low triggering and high holding voltage along with fast respond speed, which submits a robust and latch-up-immune scenario for power-rail ESD clamp circuit with SCR.

articleTitle: Characteristics of Nickel Nitride Material Grown by Reactive Magnetron Sputtering Method
abstract: This paper mainly investigates the nickel nitride compound material growth by the DC reactive magnetron sputtering technology in an Ar-N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> gas mixture with different Ar-N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> gas flow ratio and different total gas pressure respectively. The crystallization quality and thermal stability of nickel nitride were analyzed and optimized by some material characterization methods. Annealing temperature and partial pressure ratio of nitrogen results in the phase transformation of nickel nitride materials, and the total gas pressure mainly affects the crystallization quality of the materials. AFM results show that the surface roughness of Ni<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>N film grown at 3 mT is the best. XRD results show that the peak (111) of Ni film sputtering at room temperature will move to a lower diffraction peak with the increase of nitrogen content. The results of resistivity test at variable temperature show that the Ni<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>N and Ni<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>N crystals prepared by magnetron sputtering method both have good thermal stability, which can withstand an annealing temperature of about 250 degree.

articleTitle: Research on Settling Time of Decision Feedback Equalizer
abstract: Taking the setting time of decision feedback equalizer (DFE) as the point of penetration, this paper uses Simulink in MATLAB to structure a model to research on the influence of setting time of DFE. A half rate direct two tap structure is proposed, which has the advantages of simple structure and high working speed. The least mean square algorithm is optimized, which not only inherits the stability and convergence of the least mean square algorithm, but also achieves easily. The simulation results show that on the premise that the RC constant is 20*$10^{-12}$ second, when the settling time is 120ps~160ps, the eye image quality and balance effect are the best, “eye height” and “eye width” approach the ideal values of 1V and 95ps; When the settling time is 90ps~120ps, the eye image quality and balance effect are a little bad, “eye height” and “eye width” can reach 0.94V and 93.09ps at most; When the settling time is 60ps~90ps, the eye image quality and balance effect are the worst, and the maximum “eye height” and “eye width” are only 0.52V and 71.12ps. Obviously, with the increase of the settling time, the equalization effect of the DFE is strengthens, the “eye height” and “eye width” the of the output eye diagram are improved 88.46% and 33.58% separately.

articleTitle: Design of a Three-Dimensional Inlet Structure for Preventing Cell Deposition of Microfluidic Flow Cytometry
abstract: Microfluidic flow cytometry has the advantage of simple structure and easy sample handling, with a promising application for point-of-care testing. Long time imaging at low flow rates leads to inlet cell deposition and inaccurate counting. In this paper, we propose a three-dimensional inlet structure that can effectively reduce cell deposition and achieve a smaller dead zone area. First, the geometric design of the structure is presented and the flow path and dead zone distribution of the structure are analysed. Then, the design method and preparation process of the structure are described. In order to test the optimised performance of the structure, analytical experiments were carried out and cell counts were analysed and counted using image detection methods. The results show that the junction structure is able to assist in sample feeding and increase the cell throughput values by approximately 21%.

articleTitle: An efficient thermal-stress coupling design method for coaxial through silicon via
abstract: In this paper, an efficient thermal-stress coupling design method of coaxial through silicon via (TSV) is developed based on finite element method (FEM), artificial neural network (ANN) model and particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm. In order to analyze the effect of design parameters on the thermal-stress distribution of coaxial TSV, the FEM model is simulated by COMSOL. The mapping relationships between the design parameters and performance indexes are described by ANN models based on the simulation data of FEM. In addition, the multi-objective optimization criteria are formulated based on the desired performance indexes, and then the design parameters are optimized by the modified PSO algorithm. Based on the optimized design parameters, the effectiveness of the developed method is validation by FEM simulation. The simulated performance indexes well agree with the desired ones, which implies that the design parameters of coaxial TSV can be effectively optimized to control the thermal-stress distribution. Therefore, the proposed efficient thermal-stress coupling design method of coaxial TSV can achieve the thermal-stress management to improve its reliability.

articleTitle: A Modified Zener Diode-Triggered Silicon Controlled Rectifier Used for 5V Application in 0.18um BCD Process
abstract: The modified Zener diode-triggered silicon controlled rectifier (MZDTSCR) is proposed in this paper. The MZDTSCR has low trigger voltage, suitable holding voltage, low leakage current and good electrostatic discharge (ESD) robustness. The physical mechanism and results analysis of the MZDTSCR are discussed. In addition, how do the trigger and holding voltages vary with the width increasing of the N+ bridge inside the MZDTSCR, are also analyzed. Test and simulation data show that MZDTSCR can be applied to the circuit with 5V operating voltage.

articleTitle: Broadband Millimeter-Wave Frequency-Scanning Continuous Transverse Stub Array Based on SIW
abstract: A broadband millimeter-wave frequency-scanning array based on substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) is proposed in this paper. The radiation element is stepped continuous transverse stub (CTS) composed of SIW. The fed structure is a grounded coplanar waveguide (GCPW) to SIW transition line using coupling slots. The beam steering direction varies with different frequencies within the working bandwidth. One 16-element array is simulated to validate the design. The simulation results show that the relative bandwidth of S11 less than −10dB is 37.8% from 32.6 GHz to 48.1 GHz. The gain at the broadside is 18.39 dBi with the first sidelobe level of −10.2dB and the 3 dB beam width of 5.6°. The scanning angle range is from −37° to 18° depending on frequency.

articleTitle: Integration And HCI Improvement In Deep Sub-Micro CMOS process
abstract: CMOS Enhanced (CE) process derived from Logic process, The LDD implant of the I/O devices is merged into the S/D implantation. The advantage of this process is that it saves the 2 LDD Masks, While the disadvantage is the deep S/D implanting will deteriorate the performance of the core devices, and the I/O devices have high HCI reliability failure risk due to without targeted LDD. In the paper, the offset spacer (OFS) structure is implemented into 0.11um CE process to improve the HCI capability. Based on simulation and split experiment, the process conditions that can effectively reduce the performance loss of the core devices are obtained, also the effects of OFS process on devices are analyzed. Use the new process condition, the HCI capability can be greatly improved, and the performance of the core devices can meet the technical application requirement.

articleTitle: Off-State Characteristics of Polycrystalline Silicon Thin-Film Transistors under Self-Heating Stress
abstract: In this work, off-state characteristics of polycrystalline silicon (poly-Si) thin-film transistors (TFTs) under self-heating (SH) stress are tentatively studied. The difference between drain voltage and gate voltage dramatically affects the characteristics of off-state current in poly-Si TFTs. Defect generation caused by the SH effect and electric field distribution across the drain junction may be jointly responsible for the observed degradation phenomena.

articleTitle: Performance and Reliability Impact in Strained-Silicon n-LDMOS
abstract: In this brief, the dc device performance and reliability characteristics of n-type lateral double-diffused MOSFET (nLDMOS) with various operating voltages processed by the stress memorization technique are discussed. Two tensile-inducing layers, SIN and HKSION, were deposited overlaying the drift zone, accumulation region, and channel of LDMOS, respectively. Following annealing, the specific on-resistance (Ron,sp) of every LDMOS falls, although the breakdown voltage (BV) remains same. During the thermal process, the hydrogen bond formed in the tensile-inducing layer will move to the vicinity of the gate oxygen, where it will combine with Boron in the channel region, causing a 50 mV decrease in the threshold, but will be captured by the silicon hanging bonds in the accumulation region. Devices with a longer drift region have a greater likelihood of accumulation zones trapping hydrogen bonds, resulting in greater deterioration than devices with a shorter drift region. HKSION offers superior hot-carrier immunity than SIN because the majority of its hydrogen bonds are N-H bonds, which are less likely to break during the thermal process than Si-H bonds.

articleTitle: Creation of Digital Virtual Human Based on GAN2Shape and Kinect 2.0
abstract: This study aimed at the problem of the low recognition rate of facial expressions cause by complex environments. Hence, the study examined, digital virtual humans through GAN2Shape and Kinect 2.0 to obtain high-quality three-dimensional (3D) images of human faces. First, we captured and recognized facial expressions through Kinect. Second, we generated high-quality 3D images of the facial expressions through GAN2Shape and transferred the images to Unity 3D for front and back-end development to generate a facial model. Third, we recognized and captured motions through Kinect. Finally, we combined the facial model with the motions to form the virtual human model. Experimental results show that the virtual human model generated through this method has a clear face and a good effect in motion capture.

articleTitle: Electrical Properties of CrSi Thin Film Resistors for High Precision Analog Circuits
abstract: CrSi thin films are deposited on SiO2 by reactive magnetron sputtering in a mixed atmosphere of argon and nitrogen, where nitrogen is the reactive gas, following by annealing in nitrogen and hydrogen at different temperatures. The effects of sputtering atmosphere (nitrogen flow rate) and annealing temperature on film structural and electrical properties of these films are investigated. It’s found that nitrogen doping inhibits grains growth to a certain extent and the effects of nitrogen doping amount on the square resistance of annealed films are different. TCR (temperature coefficient of resistance), by adjusting the sputtering atmosphere and annealing temperature, can be effectively controlled within the original 10% range, that is, optimized from about ±20 ppm/ ℃ to ±2 ppm/ ℃, indicating that resistors possess more excellent stability performance. This work probes the impact trend of key process parameters on square resistance and TCR in detail, which have important reference value for the development of high-precision resistors technology.

articleTitle: Enhancement-mode AlGaN/GaN HEMTs with a semi-wraparound metal-insulator-semiconductor gate
abstract: In this work, p-GaN gate HEMTs with a semi-wraparound metal-insulator-semiconductor (MIS) gate are investigated. By using SiN and gate metal to surround the p-GaN layer, the output current of the p-GaN gate HEMTs has been increased from 11.4 mA/mm to 15.2 mA/mm, with a high threshold voltage of 8.1 V. The on-state resistance has been reduced from $166.7 m\Omega \cdot mm$ to $97.0 m\Omega \cdot mm$. The peak transconductance error bars show an increase in the average transconductance of the samples from 4.4 mS to 5.5 mS. The breakdown characteristic shows an increase in breakdown voltage from 174 V to 207 V, demonstrating the effectiveness of this method in improving the DC characteristics of p-GaN gate HEMTs.

articleTitle: Lens-free microfluidic-based method for detecting circulating tumor cells
abstract: Accurate identification of Circulating tumor cells (CTCs) can provide valuable information for early diagnosis and therapeutic monitoring of cancer. Here, we present a method of lens-free imaging combined with microfluidic technology to accomplish label-free classification of CTCs and blood cells (BCs). In this approach, Cell images in a microfluidic chip are recorded and classification of the images is accomplished using a Yolo-V4 convolutional neural network. The recognition precision of CTCs and BCs reached 99.21% and 98.26%, respectively. The 8 microfluidic channels used allow a high throughput of 70,000 cells per minute without clogging. It can be seen that the method has great advantages in detecting rare cells.

articleTitle: Design of Anti-irradiation Latch Based on Triple Module Redundancy Technology
abstract: As the feature size of CMOS technology continues to decrease, the critical charge of circuits also decreases, making them more sensitive to single-event effects (SEEs). Traditional triple module redundancy (TMR) latches are resilient to single-node upset (SNU) and double-node upset (DNU), but they do not consider CLK signal flip (multi-point flip) which brings multiple concerns regarding reliability. In this paper, we propose a novel anti-irradiation TMR latch structure. The master latch is reinforced to enhance its tolerance to input signal upset, internal node upset, and CLK signal upset. The voting circuit is reinforced with double redundancy to improve the tolerance of the system to SNU and DNU. We conduct single-particle injection simulations using the HSPICE model with a double-exponential current source based on a 55-nm CMOS technology. The simulation results indicate that the proposed latch structure enhances the anti-irradiation performance and can tolerate SNU, DNU, and CLK signal flip.

articleTitle: A real scene interactive augmented reality glasses based on head locating and pose measuring
abstract: In this paper, we added a head locating and pose measuring device into a self-produced augmented reality (AR) glasses. The output content is based on integral imaging technology, which enables the display of 3D content. The head locating and pose measuring device can drive the lens combination to rotate the phase angle, so that the wearer can view three-dimensional objects with different viewing angles without changing the displayed information. Such a design allows the wearer to continuously change the depth of focus for observation within a certain depth range, which greatly alleviates the discomfort caused by traditional AR glasses.

articleTitle: Modulation the properties of MoTe₂-based inverter by phase transition engineering
abstract: Phase transition from the semiconducting hexagonal (2H) phase to the metallic monoclinic (IT’) phase in two-dimensional (2D) transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) like MoTe₂ is not only of great importance in fundamental study but also of technological significance for broad device applications. In this paper, we demonstrate a method for modulating the performance of complementary inverters based on transformation engineering by laser burning. The performance of the inverter is compared by phase transition of MoTe₂ in different regions of the MoTe2-MoS2 heterostructure complementary inverter heterostructure (i.e. electrode and channel regions), and it is found that the gain of the inverter after the phase transformation at the electrode region is higher. The proposed method to control the function of complementary inverters by laser phase transition is of great significance for the application of two-dimensional materials in logic devices.

articleTitle: High performance Graphene photodetectors decorat ed by semi-metal nanoparticles
abstract: Two-dimensiona1(2D) Graphene has receive d much research interest because of its special optical an d electronic characteristics. However, due to the atomic thickness, single-layer Graphene absorbs only 2.3% of the incident light in the visible and near-infrared regions, which restrict the practical application of Graphene in the field of photodetectors. The strong resonant absorption of plasmonic nanostructures can enhance the light-matter interaction, which is expected to enhance the photodetect ion performance of Graphene. Here, we propose and pre pare the Graphene photodetectors decorated by W$\mathrm{O}_{\mathrm{x}(\mathrm{x}\lt3)}$ semi-metal nanoparticles with the localized surface plasmonic effect (LSPR). The W$\mathrm{O}_{\mathrm{x}(\mathrm{x}\lt3)}$ semi-metal nanoparticles possess strong LSPR, and thus make the interaction between thin-layer Graphene and incident light greatly enhanced. The photoelectric performance of the Graphene photodetector is therefore significantly improved. The W$\mathrm{O}_{\mathrm{x}}-$Graphene composite structure based photodetectors under visible laser illumination exhibit highly photoresponsivity and detectivity. This obvious enhancement of photoelectric performance benefits predominately from t he hot electron transfer caused by the LSPR effect excite d via the semi-metal nanoparticles.

articleTitle: Research and Practice on the Verification of the Suitability of high Purity Alumina Substrates for Aerospace Processes
abstract: This article proposes a new verification technique that meets the requirements of in-orbit processes by detailed analysis, covers the entire process of circuit processing and assembly applications, and closely combines standard test methods with simulated working conditions. Through the practice and analysis of typical test items such as thin film adhesion and substrate bending strength, the focus and verification details of the process suitability verification process are clarified. The verification results show that the test standards and test methods should be in line with the application conditions, and the verification methods should also be implemented in conjunction with the actual process conditions, in order to make scientific judgments.

articleTitle: Deposition of High-K Al2O3 Dielectric Films on Graphene via Atomic Layer Deposition for Fabrication of High Transparent Capacitors
abstract: In this work, the high transparent capacitors have been prepared on quartz substrates by using graphene as the bottom electrodes. The dense Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> films deposited on the treated surface of graphene by atomic layer deposition (ALD) are served as the dielectric layer of the capacitors. Here. The aluminum-doped zinc oxide (AZO) films are in situ grown on the Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> dielectric by ALD as the top electrodes. The capacitors show that the maximal capacitance is 3.33 fF/u$\mathrm{m}^{2}$ at 10 kHz and the minimum leakage current is $6.3\times 10^{-s}$A/$\mathrm{cm}^{2}$ at 1 V. The graphene-based capacitors are in possession of an average optical transmittance of over 80 %, thus as good candidates for integration in transparent circuits.

articleTitle: Bandpass Power Divider Module Based on Integrated Passive Fabrication Process
abstract: In the field of modern microwave radio frequency application, power divider is an important integrated passive device (IPD) to realize signal matching, power distribution, frequency band selection and filtering, etc. There is also a higher demand for miniaturization and low cost in the market. In this paper, a miniaturized bandpass power divider module is designed on the GaAs substrate based on the IPD fabrication process, which realizes the power equalization function in a specific frequency range and has good out-of-band rejection characteristics. The band-pass power divider module is integrated by a high-pass filter, a low-pass filter, a coupler, and a combiner, with a compact structure having a chip area of 4.8 mm $\times$ 1.8 mm $\times$ 0.22 mm. It can achieve a fourth-order bandpass frequency response with transmission zeros at 0.4 GHz and 3.4 GHz on both sides of the passband. The center frequency of the bandpass response is 1.5 GHz, and the fractional bandwidth is about 40% between 1 GHz to 2 GHz. The insertion loss is 4.7 dB, and the return loss and isolation are better than −15dB and −18dB, respectively. Simulation results indicate the proposed bandpass power divider can achieve equal power division, which has the characteristics of wide frequency band, high isolation, low insertion loss and miniaturization. Transmission zero effectively improves the roll-off factor of the passband and the out-of-band rejection, enhancing the performance of out-of-band filtering and selectivity.

articleTitle: Absorption Markov Lifetime Evaluation Model Based on Weibull Distribution
abstract: Lifetime test is an important part of integrated circuit reliability research. The lifetime of samples can be theoretically evaluated through lifetime test. However, the current lifetime evaluation is mostly carried out through a large amount of empirical and historical data accumulation, which requires a mass of time and economic cost. In this paper, the lifetime of the sample can be theoretically deduced from a small amount of data by absorption Markov chain based on Weibull distribution.

articleTitle: A photovoltaic-wind hybrid energy system for herdsmen with considering bad weather conditions
abstract: The weather changes have a large impact on users of hybrid-micro-grid-system (HMGS). In this paper, a photovoltaic-wind hybrid energy system with considering bad weather conditions is presented to meet the energy demand of herdsman’s home in Qinghai Province and mitigate the impact of weather changes on user experience. The simulation results using Matlab/SIMULINK indicate that the system can generate about 14.997 - 1S.559 kWh electricity in one day. The system provides users with the advised-operating-time (ADOT) of the appliances to lessen the impact of weather changes. The experimental results show that the system can provide users with a lot of instructive information to improve user experience.

articleTitle: Capacitive Tuning Effects on the Vertical T-coil Broadband ESD Protection Circuit
abstract: The vertical T-coil broadband ESD protection circuits have the advantage of very small area. However, due to the process variation and the lack of precise models for the multi-layer helical inductors, the actual performance of the vertical T-coil broadband ESD protection circuit could deviate from the one estimated at the design stage. In this paper, we present an improved circuit with tunability and investigate the effectiveness of the capacitive tuning structure on improving and optimizing the frequency characteristics of the circuit.

articleTitle: Fourier Ptychography-based VCSEL array spots imaging quality enhancement
abstract: The Vertical-Cavity Surface-Emitting Laser (VCSEL) is a promising laser source in the optical communication and 3-D sensing for its low threshold current, low power consumption and fast data throughput. To assess the performance of the VCSEL chip, the near-field and far field spots of VCSEL are recorded via an optical microscopic system to calculate the parameters such as uniformity, energy, divergence angle and so on. However, the VCSEL spot analysis of the near field requires extremely high resolution whereas the current detector or the optical system can barely satisfy this demand. To this end, the author applies one method referred as Fourier Ptychography (FP), which is a phase retrieval algorithm merging redundant information into a high spatial band product result, aiming to enhance the near-field VCSEL spot resolution to achieve more accurate parameters. By rotating the illumination angle of VCSEL, multiple angle-varied spot information is captured, then apply FP to fetch an enhanced spot image. Experiment results indicate that our method can greatly improve the spot imaging quality and be of some help for the data analysis.

articleTitle: An Adjustable Ramp Voltage Circuit for a Large Array of Capacitive Loads
abstract: In current image sensor circuits, the traditional ramp circuit shows the problems of low precision of adjustable slope and insufficient driving ability when facing a large array. This paper proposes a high-precision and high-driving adjustable ramp voltage circuit for the image sensor, including a bandgap reference voltage source, a current mirror array, and a buffer driver. The reference current in the proposed adjustable ramp circuit adopts a high-precision bandgap design, and a buffer driver circuit is added to ensure the slope accuracy. Meanwhile, the output terminal adopts a push-pull structure. Simulation results in a 65 nm CMOS process show that the proposed adjustable ramp generation circuit can drive a large array of capacitive loads with a ramp voltage range from 1 V to 5 V and an adjustable slope range from 6 $\mu$s to 60 $\mu$s. The adjustable ramp circuit can achieve 1-10 dynamic adjustments, and a large array of capacitive loads can be driven when dynamic adjustment is achieved. Compared with the traditional resistance or capacitance adjustable circuit, the slope accuracy increases by 20%, and the driving ability of the proposed adjustable ramp circuit increases by 61.35%.

articleTitle: A 10-Gb/s Low-noise and Low-crosstalk Transimpedance Amplifier Designed in 130-nm BiCMOS
abstract: In this paper, we propose a 10Gb/s pseudo-differential Trans-impedance Amplifier (TIA) for the high-speed receiver, which employs the inductive-peaking technique to improve the noise performance and bandwidth, and a low-crosstalk Electrostatic Discharge (ESD) architecture to improve the crosstalk immunity of the receiver. The whole receiver circuit which implemented in 130-nm Bipolar Complementary Metal Oxide Semiconductor (BiCMOS) includes a low-crosstalk ESD, a pseudo-differential TIA, a Direct Current Offset Correction (DCOC), a single-ended to differential converter (S2D) and an output buffer (OB). The simulated bandwidth and transimpedance gain of receiver are 8.5 GHz and 70 dB $\Omega$, respectively, and the input reference RMS noise is 1326nA with a 200fF photodiode. Moreover, the simulation results show that the supply noise rejection ratio is improved by 25dB @ 5GHz with the proposed ESD architecture. The total current of the pseudo-differential TIA is 7. 14mA under 3. 3V supply.

articleTitle: Process optimization of Flatness of LTCC Substrate for TR Module
abstract: Flatness is one of the important indicators for evaluating LTCC (low temperature co-fired ceramic) substrates. Unqualified flatness will cause the substrate to crack during the welding process, which will seriously affect the reliability of the subsequent assembly. In this paper, studying of the co-fired process and analysing the method of optimising the flatness of LTCC substrates, a TR component substrate of LTCC was used as the technology carrier, and a pressure co-firing process was developed innovatively to optimise the flatness and distortion of the substrate by studying the material of pressed burnt matter, the weight ratio of pressed burnt matter to the blank which to be pressed and fired and the effect on shrinkage rates, and the reliability of the surface layer of the substrate after co-firing was verified. The results provide a feasible solution to the flatness problem of LTCC substrate and can be extended and applied to the process route of all subsequent LTCC products with warpage risk, solving the bottleneck process problems of common LTCC substrates in the co-fire process, improving the reliability of subsequent assembly.

articleTitle: Generic Memory Modeling with Recurrent Neural Network
abstract: In this work, a methodology for developing a memory compact model is described using recurrent neural network (RNN). Compared to traditional modeling approaches, it is flexible and able to develop an accurate model based on physical data before the material physics is fully understood. A simple ReRAM-type memory model is demonstrated using Nonlinear Autoregressive with External Input (NARX) machine learning approach. To enable the neural network to capture the resistive switching characteristics of ReRAM, the output at a range of cycling voltages was captured and used as training data. The trained model is used for DC prediction under different voltage amplitudes, and the prediction results are consistent with the physical data, with MSE values below $10^{-9}$. The accuracy of the RNN-assisted ReRAM model during the read, write and erase operations is also evaluated to show the validity of the approach. The calibration between the prediction results of the model and experimental data further proves the feasibility of the approach.

articleTitle: Rapid Generation of Physical Holograms Based on Light Fields
abstract: Light field cameras can capture the direction and intensity of light to achieve “photograph first and then focus holographic display is a future-oriented 3D display technology, both light field and holography technology focus on recording three-dimensional information of objects. In this paper, we try to combine light field with holographic display, and use light field image combined with deep learning algorithm to generate physical hologram quickly. Aiming at the problem of low resolution of light field sub-images, the super-resolution algorithm is used to improve the resolution, and then the depth estimation algorithm is used to estimate the corresponding depth information, as well as a pair of RGB-D images, and the RGB-D images are input to the neural network to generate holograms. Experimental results show that the network can quickly generate high-quality, high-resolution holograms, and well reflect scene depth information during reconstruction.

articleTitle: SoC Design of ECG Intelligent Classification
abstract: Every year, many people die of cardiovascular disease around the world, even though most of this disease can be effectively prevented at an early stage. Traditional heart rhythm monitoring methods rely on doctors, resulting in poor real-time performance. This paper designs a System-on-Chip (SoC) targeting at the electrocardiography (ECG) intelligent classification. Real-time heart rhythm monitoring brought by artificial intelligence (AI) can effectively help catch the early treatment. A Deep Neural Network (DNN) model is adopted to classify the four common categories of heart rhythms. The test results show that the DNN model used in this paper manages to classify the four common heart rhythm categories with a correct rate of 96.4%. In order to accelerate the operation process, the system contains a specific coprocessor running the complex operation process of DNN. The coprocessor and the central processing unit (CPU) interconnect with each other by Nuclei Instruction Co-unit Extension (NICE) bus. Finally, a 40-time increase in the system operation speed is achieved. Meanwhile, the hardware logic resource consumption is reduced by about 32% through quantizing the model parameters from 32-bit floating-point number into 16-bit fixed-point number.

articleTitle: Broadband and Low Loss Directional Coupler Based on GaAs-IPD Technology for C-Band Application
abstract: In this paper, a directional coupler is achieved through first-order and second-order circuit structures based on GaAs integrated passive manufacturing process. Based on the circuit structure of the proposed novel symmetric topology, different topologies and corresponding transmission characteristics can be obtained by using the odd-even mode analysis on it. The first-order directional coupler operates from 0.4 GHz to 1.4 GHz, with insertion loss <0.5 dB, return loss > −15 dB, coupling < −20 dB, isolation < −50 dB, and the size is 1.4 mm $\times 1.3$ mm $\times 0.2$ mm. The second-order directional coupler operates from 3 GHz to 8 GHz, insertion loss < 0.5 dB, return loss > −20 dB, coupling <−20 dB, isolation > −60 dB, the size is 1.5 mm $\times 1.3$ mm $\times 0.2$ mm. This work realizes quantitative power distribution and measurement and monitoring of desired signals in a wide frequency band with low loss, which can improve the integration of microwave integrated circuits.

articleTitle: D-shaped Micro-structured Optical Fiber Based Surface Plasmon Resonance Sensor with High Sensitivity at Low Refractive Index
abstract: A novel D-shaped micro-structured optical fiber (MOF) based surface plasmon resonance (SPR) sensor is designed and numerically investigated, to solve the problem of low sensitivity at the RI range below 1.33 of fiber SPR sensors. By depositing a gold layer on a semicircular ring-shaped channel at the top of the fiber to excite SPR, the RI sensitivity of the sensor can reach 13300 nm/RIU at 1.25, with the resolution of $7.52\times 10^{-6}$ RIU. The RI sensing range can be extended to as low as 1.17 with high sensitivity, which can be used for some low RI analytes detection such as the anesthetic sevoflurane, medical oxygen, and liquid carbon dioxide.

articleTitle: A Fluorescent-Based POCT System for Blood Cell Testing
abstract: Point-of-care testing has developed rapidly in recent years and is widely used in all clinical and home examinations. However, Point-of-care Equipment is unwieldy and time-consuming to detect the blood cell concentration. In this paper, we have proposed a low-cost and rapid system for detecting the concentration of specific particles using fluorescence detection technology. The system consists of a container, an excitation part and an emission part. The excitation and emission are in two different planes. And the system achieves a better signal-to-noise ratio by this construction. The fluorescent microbeads were used as samples to test the system. The measurement using the system is fast, low cost and suitable for clinical blood cell concentration testing.

articleTitle: Design of Beveled Edge Termination in GaN Vertical p-i-n Diodes: A Simulation Study
abstract: Various electric field profile simulations are carried to design the vertical gallium nitride (GaN) p-i-n diodes with negative beveled edge termination to optimize breakdown voltage. Although traditional beveled edge termination can also be used to alleviate the fringe electric field crowding effect and obtain a breakdown voltage comparable with the parallel plane ideal case, a larger length of the edge termination is required. In this paper, we introduced a two-step beveled edge termination structure to save the area used to improve the breakdown voltage, which can reduce 83% of the termination length required to achieve 90% of the ideal breakdown voltage. Through TCAD simulation, the higher doping concentration ratio between the P-GaN and the drift layer is, the shorter the depth of the mesa and the longer edge termination are needed to achieve the same percentage of the ideal breakdown voltage. The two-step beveled edge termination could save more area if the Mg concentration in P-GaN is larger. This structure and the rule explored in this paper has significance for the design of GaN-based p-i-n diodes with high breakdown voltage and small area.

articleTitle: Preparation of RGO and CNT Composite Thin Film Electrode for Flexible Energy Storage Devices
abstract: Recently, miniaturized systems with multiple functionalities, such as such as flexibility, self-powering and sensing capability are urgently desired for the practical applications. In this work, we reported the fabrication of novel reduced graphene oxide and carbon nanotube based composite electrode on the flexible polyimide substrate and explored its physical and electrochemical properties. The proposed composite electrode shows superior properties, such as high flexibility, high surface area, low inner resistance, as well as a high specific capacitance of 208.7 mF/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, and energy density of 5.33 mWh/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, indicating its great potential in the integrated supercapacitor and sensor applications.

articleTitle: Design of low phase noise wide frequency range ring voltage controlled oscillator
abstract: Based on 0.18$\mu$m CMOS technology, a low phase noise and wide frequency range ring voltage controlled oscillator (RVCO) used in the clock generation circuit of a 10 M/100Mbps on-board Ethernet PHY chip is designed. Negative Skew was used to reduce the pull up time of the transition process and the value of the pulse sensitive function, thus reducing the phase noise of CMOS RVCO. At the same time, an active inductive load was used to realize wide range frequency tuning. The post-simulation results show that when the power supply voltage is 1. 8V, the tuning voltage range is OV to 1. 4V, the frequency range is 80MHz to 528MHz, the Kvco is -475MHz/V, the phase noise -112.05dBc/Hz and average current disspation is about 1. 5mA when the target frequency is 200 MHz.

articleTitle: New Bidirectional Silicon-Controlled Rectifier for Low-Voltage ESD Protection
abstract: Electrostatic discharge (ESD) protection is an important issue for the modern integrated circuits (ICs). As for the input/output (I/O) pins having a varying operating voltage in the positive and negative ranges, the traditional diode or GGNMOS architecture is not applicable, making the corresponding ESD design more difficult. Among the several widely used ESD protection devices, the silicon-controlled rectifier (SCR) has a high ESD robustness. However, it should be further optimized to decrease its trigger voltage and meet the requirement for the bidirectional applications. In this paper, a new modified diode triggered bidirectional SCR is proposed, the layout area is reduced by commonly using the trigger diode. The clamp voltage is also reduced by changing the locations of the active regions. The proposed device was fabricated in a 28 nm CMOS technology. The experimental results show that the new proposed device has a symmetry I-V characteristic and a good ESD robustness.

articleTitle: A High Dynamic Range Pulse Frequency Modulation ADC for Ambient Light Sensor
abstract: In this paper, we propose a high dynamic range pulse frequency modulation (PFM) analog-to-digital converter (ADC) with adjustable range for ambient light detection, which employs a buffered direct injection(BDI) input stage circuit to improve the low injection efficiency of the traditional input stage PFM ADC under weak illumination, and a digital range control circuit and current divider to improve the dynamic range loss and non-linearity caused by the residual charge of the integrating capacitor and the reset loop delay. The ADC circuit was designed in a 0.35-$\mu \mathrm{m}$ CMOS process. The simulation results show that the dynamic range of the ADC is more than 132dB, the maximum operating current is $8.7\mu \mathrm{A}$, and the maximum non-linearity is only 0.113% under 3. 3V supply.

articleTitle: High-performance Non-porous P(VDF-TrFE) Film Preparation and Its Application to Flexible RF Devices
abstract: P(VDF-TrFE) has a good potential for flexible electronics application owing to its good piezoelectric performance and excellent flexibility. However, high density of pores and large surface roughness of the material cause the high loss of acoustic waves, limiting its use in bulk acoustic devices. In this paper, a simple method is proposed to effectively remove the pores inside the P(VDF-TrFE) film and reduce the surface roughness yet maintaining the piezoelectric properties of the film. The obtained thin film possesses excellent properties and characteristics: much improved breakdown strength of >300kV/mm; very high $\beta-$phase content, >80% and extraordinarily high piezoelectric coefficients, d<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">33</inf>=S0pm/V. By utilizing this high-performance film, we have successfully fabricated flexible FBAR devices and obtained good performance.

articleTitle: Nanoscale Failure Analysis of an Aluminium Alloy for Space Applications
abstract: This study has used focused ion beam (FIB) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) to investigate the corrosion behaviour of AA7108 alloy at nanoscale. The high-resolution characterization allowed the analysis of microstructure evolution during corrosion process from microscale to nanoscale. This provides previously unseen details of trenching corrosion. For example, the dealloying of Fe-containing particle occurs immediately with the initiation of trenching corrosion. Based on these details, the relevant corrosion mechanisms are proposed.

articleTitle: The Correlation of Total Dose Effect and Hot Carrier Injection for Radiation Hardened MOS
abstract: In this article, the 1.8V NMOS transistors prepared by the radiation hardened 0.18$\mu$m process has well radiation resistance. There is no shift of threshold voltage and off-state current after irradiating at 500 krad(Si). Compared to the radiation-hardened NMOS transistor without irradiating, the degradation of radiation-hardened transistor is worse after TID and HCI. The HCI damage of the radiation-hardened NMOS transistor is slightly worse than that of standard process, which may be due to the reason that the P-type impurity concentration in the region under STI field increased by radiation-hardened process reduced the channel width. The HCI reliability of the radiation-hardened NMOS transistor is greater than 0.2 years @ 1.1Vdd.

articleTitle: Evaluation by Simulation of Quasi-vertical GaN Schottky Barrier Diode With Trench Floating Metal Rings
abstract: This paper proposes the trench floating metal ring (TR-FMR) as a novel terminal structure to improve the breakdown voltage (BV) of quasi-vertical GaN Schottky barrier diode (SBD). TR-FMR can disperse the electric field in both horizontal and vertical directions and introduces a new electric field peak into the GaN drift layer, which can make full use of drift layer to withstand voltage. The simulation results show that, compared with PL-FMR, the breakdown of TRFMR SBDs with one metal ring is increased by 180 V, twice than conventional SBD. The depletion region widths at horizontal and vertical directions are larger than PL-FMR, achieving a more uniform electric field distribution. Moreover, the BV can increase with the number of rings increasing, reaching 670 V for three rings. The TR-FMR terminal structure shows great promise for quasi-vertical GaN SBD.

articleTitle: Demonstration of Ultra-Fine RDLs Interposer Fabricated by Organic Dielectric CMP Process
abstract: To address the rapid growing huge data communication demand, the fabrication of high density and high speed interconnect link has become more and more important in the integration of semiconductor chips. For example, redistribution layer (RDL) with feature size below 5 microns is more and more popular in the lasted heterogeneous integration technology. However, traditional semi-additive process cannot deal with RDL with ultra-fine pitch and via opening. Therefore, new solutions for ultra-fine interconnect link to meet the ever-increasing data transmission demands are required.In this paper, we demonstrated a method to fabricate multi-layer RDL interposer by the organic dielectric chemical mechanical planarization (CMP) process. In the RDL interposer, the minimum line/space of 2/2 microns is presented, and the minimum via diameter is 15 microns. Furthermore, the planarization for both organic dielectric and copper line is demonstrated. The CMP process can also help to suppress the warpage conditions, which is crucial to the success of producing process. By the advantages of our method, we consider it can make great achievements in the field of heterogeneous integration with bandwidth data communication.

articleTitle: Nondestructive Inspection Techniques Based on Millimeter Wave Machine and A-priori Algorithm
abstract: As a nondestructive and convenient technology, through-wall detection has played an essential role in many fields, such as construction, fire protection, and public security. This research proposes a new method for radar, which gives a hypothetical value of the data inverted by known information after obtaining the measurement data from radar and infrared detectors. It introduces an error matrix in the calculation process, which reduces the error of the data calculated by specific millimeter wave intensity detection method. The method proposed in this paper avoids the identification difficulties caused by errors and forms a joint inversion mechanism of microwave and near infrared with applicability and controllable error range, which is improved on the basis of an a-priori iterative operator. Considering that electromagnetic field inverse scattering has the problems of nonconvergence and significant error, this study aims to establish a subsurface analysis system with small result intervals through an emerging arithmetic iteration a-priori technique in the computer field. The method can also be applied to other fields of millimeter wave detection through inheriting, synthesizing, and innovating based on traditional algorithms in multisource information fusion, a-priori knowledge, inversion theory, and feature recognition.

articleTitle: Research Progress and Prospect of Silicon-Based RF Microsystems
abstract: Silicon based RF microsystem has great application potential in radar/communication and other fields. In this paper, several typical microsystem products are developed by using silicon-based wafer level 3D stacking technology, the integration and production efficiency are greatly improved, thus providing a solution for the large-scale manufacturing of advanced RF products.

articleTitle: Compact Broadband Balanced Filter Based on Integrated Passive Process
abstract: In this paper, we propose a compact, broadband balanced filter based on integrated passive process (IPD), which can realize the balanced-unbalanced conversion of microwave signal. The proposed balanced filter is composed of a band-pass filter and a balun, the former selects the working frequency band for the balanced filter, and the latter realizes the conversion of the signal. Simulation results show that the specific operation frequency band of the balanced filter is 2.8 GHz to 4.8 GHz, the insertion loss of the two output ports at the center frequency of 4.37 GHz is −1.514dB and −1.541dB respectively, the phase difference is 180.9°, and the center frequency is within the range of 500 MHz. The insertion loss of the two output ports does not exceed −2.5dB, the maximum difference between the insertion loss of the two ports is about 1 dB, the phase difference fluctuates up and down by ±5°, and the overall size is approximately 1250 $\mu {\mathrm {m}} \times 1250 \mu$m. It has the advantages of compact structure, low loss, frequency bandwidth, low phase deviation, it can be suitable for applications in communication, RF front-end, Bluetooth, WiFi, GPS navigation and other fields.

articleTitle: An ultra-high sensitivity optical thermometer based on NaYF₄:Yb³⁺, Nd³⁺ nanomaterials
abstract: In recent years, improving the sensitivity of optical thermometers has been a research hotspot. In this paper, an ultra-high sensitivity optical thermometer based on NaYF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>:Yb,Nd nanomaterials is investigated. With increasing temperature, the infrared light intensity and visible light intensity exhibited opposite temperature dependence under 980 nm laser excitation. In the temperature range of 323-523K, based on the fluorescence intensity ratio (FIR) technique, the temperature dependence of the FIR between emission peaks is studied, and the relative ($\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{A}}$) and absolute sensitivity ($\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{R}}$) are obtained. It is found that the maximum SA reaches 92.78 $\mathrm{K}^{-1}$, and the maximum SR reaches 16.28 %$\mathrm{K}^{-1}$. These excellent properties make NaYF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>:Yb<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup>, $\mathrm{Nd}^{3+}$ nanomaterials will be used in high-precision optical thermometers.

articleTitle: New Compatible Stress-Complementary BCD Technology for Deep Trench Isolation
abstract: A new compatible stress-compensated bipolar-CMOS-DMOS (C-SC BCD) technique is proposed and experimentally proved in this letter. Based on the conventional BCD technology, C-SC introduces three steps of back etching, back sealing and front sealing, and is fully compatible with the BCD process. C-SC can gradually relieve and compensate the stress introduced by the deep trench isolation structure of thick film silicon-on-insulator (SOI) devices. The mechanism of C-SC technology lies in the reasonable distribution of thermal stress, tensile stress and compressive stress, which makes the stress acting on the wafer compensate each other and greatly reduces the original significant wafer bow. Verified by experiments on SOI and silicon materials with different thicknesses, surface bow caused by deep trench isolation structure is almost eliminated after using C-SC technology. The C-SC technology is demonstrated by experiments of a SOI with 1S $\mu \mathrm{m}$ silicon and 3.5 $\mu \mathrm{m}$ the buried oxide layer (BOX) layer, which revealed that the C-SC BCD technology can reduce the probability of online anomalies and improve the uniformity of devices and integrated circuits on the wafer.

articleTitle: A 8.9 ppm/°C Voltage Reference with Piecewise Curvature Compensation
abstract: In this paper, a novel MOS-only voltage reference with curvature compensation is proposed. The proposed circuit using NMOS self-cascode composite transistors (SCCT) and gate-source voltage of NMOS transistor. The compensation circuit achieves piecewise voltage adjustment. It reduces the temperature coefficient (TC) of the voltage reference. The circuit is designed and simulated using 0.18$\mu$m CMOS process. The simulation results show that the supply voltage range of the voltage reference is 1-2.5V, and the linear regulation (LR) is 0.77 %/V; At the conditions of TT process corner and supply voltage of 1.8 V, the typical current consumption is 0.27 $\mu$A. The circuit achieved a temperature coefficient of 8.9 ppm/°C from −50°C to 125°C. The circuit can be widely used in low-power chips such as implantable biomedical and Internet of Things (IoT) chips
